title: Hardware matrix regression + hybrid load harness for tokens/sec and p95 drift detection
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build a unified benchmarking and load-testing harness that runs a hardware matrix (A10, L4, A100, H100) across representative workloads and detects regressions in tokens/sec, p95 latency, and cost-per-token. The harness must support both synthetic load and production trace replay, capture percentiles and tail latencies, compute cost-per-token with amortized GPU-hour + infra overhead, and integrate with CI/GitHub checks and nightly baselines. Goal: automated regression alerts and PR gates that prevent shipping perf regressions without manual signoff.
acceptance_criteria: A distributed runner executes benchmarks against A10,L4,A100,H100 with a single job spec and emits tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99, QPS, and per-request cost estimates
Regression detection algorithm runs for each model+hardware and flags when p95 increases >15% and statistical test (ADWIN or z-score) indicates drift across 3 consecutive nightly runs
Cost-per-token calculator produces a CSV and dashboard with cost breakdown (GPU amortization, power, network, storage, infra overhead) and sample per-token numbers for short/medium/long sequences
CI integration: PRs touching runtime or kernel-selection add a check that runs a fast smoke harness and fails PR if a P0 regression threshold is crossed
Golden baselines stored in s3://redwood-bench/baselines/ and versioned by runtime-1.18+model+date, with tooling to roll forward baselines after manual review
Grafana dashboard and alerting rule created: alert when nightly regression severity >= medium for production-facing models
steps: Design job spec format that decouples model, sequence distribution, concurrency, and kernel flags
Implement loadgen adapter that can do (a) synthetic token-level throughput with fixed seq length distributions and (b) replay of sampled production traces anonymized
Instrument runtime to emit per-request token counts and precise latency histograms (hdrhistogram) and a lightweight per-batch cost estimator
Implement cost-per-token module: fetch instance hourly price, amortize GPU-hour across measured usable tokens/sec*run_seconds, add power/EPS estimate, and add fixed infra margin

Implement regression detection service: run nightly, compute percent-change and statistical test (ADWIN drift detector + z-score comparison), produce summarized report and regression ticket if threshold crossed
Hook up results to GH checks and Concourse/CircleCI nightly jobs; publish results to s3 and update Grafana
Create runbooks: how to triage a detected regression and steps to roll back or run targeted experiments
metrics: Primary: tokens/sec (measured per model+hardware at target concurrency)
Latency: p50/p90/p95/p99 token generation latency and end-to-end request latency
Cost: estimated $/token and $/1M tokens broken down by GPU amortization / power / infra
Stability: standard deviation across runs, EWMA of tokens/sec, ADWIN drift indicator
Regression gates: percent change in p95, z-score, consecutive-run count
